issues.body: require_one_side_bound is still a standalone helper whose documentation tells callers to run it before wire::derive_grants. No changed production boundary invokes it, while the acceptance tests call the helper directly. Controller-authored rule text can therefore still reach derive_grants without the claimed fail-closed seeding check.
issues.fix_hint: Enforce require_one_side_bound at the shared production boundary where controller-authored .acr text enters derive_grants/evaluation, propagate denial fail-closed, and add an integration test that submits both unseeded and seeded rules through that real path. Alternatively, consistently narrow all public claims to describe an optional static-analysis helper and leave operational enforcement explicitly unresolved.
issues.title: Fail-closed seeding guard remains unenforced on the real .acr path

issues.body: is_var still recognizes only terms beginning with '?', so term_bound treats an N3 blank-node label such as '_:x' as a bound constant. Such a label is formula-scoped/existential rather than an externally fixed endpoint and cannot conservatively provide the promised constant-side lookup. For example, `{ _:x p:linkedTo ?o } => { ?o p:ok p:v }` can pass incorrectly.
issues.fix_hint: Treat blank-node labels as formula-scoped unbound terms for seeding analysis, or reject them as unsupported. Add a require_one_side_bound regression test proving a blank-node-labelled endpoint cannot seed an otherwise unbound atom.
issues.title: Blank-node labels are still incorrectly accepted as constant seeds

verdict.summary: Round 5 is stagnant. Both round-4 major findings remain in the submitted diff. The seeding guard is still only an optional public helper documented for callers to invoke; no production .acr admission/derive_grants boundary enforces it, and the acceptance suite exercises the helper directly rather than the real controller-rule path. Blank-node labels also remain accepted as constant seeds because is_var recognizes only '?' variables. The feature-matrix leg improves execution coverage but does not repair either correctness gap.
